complexity.notes: The lands counter is dead code: it is computed and decremented but never read, since termination is driven by the row scan. Two things make this quadratic rather than linear: the linear membership test q not in queue on every neighbor check, and rescanning the grid from row 0 to locate each new island (up to O(n) scan work per island). ||Marking a cell as visited when it is enqueued, rather than when it is popped, removes the need for the membership test entirely and restores O(n).|| The border-padding rewrite is a neat way to avoid bounds checks, though it copies the whole grid; iterating neighbors with index arithmetic would avoid that.
complexity.summary: Pads the grid with a water border, then repeatedly scans rows for a remaining '1' and flood-fills that island with an explicit-stack DFS, zeroing cells as they are popped and counting one island per fill.
